nodes.text: Run proton NMR spectra to gather structural information
Run carbon NMR spectra
Proton NMR shows 4 methyl groups (all singlets, 12H total), no coupling, likely attached to quaternary or sp2 carbons

support.quote:
The proton NMR shows:
- 1.78 ppm (s, 3H) - singlet, 3 protons
- 1.92 ppm (s, 6H) - singlet, 6 protons
- 2.65 ppm (s, 3H) - singlet, 3 protons

Total: 12 protons, all appearing as singlets. This suggests:
- No coupling between protons (all singlets)
- Likely methyl groups attached to quaternary carbons or heteroatoms

nodes.text: Carbon NMR has 3 sp2/aromatic carbons (161.40, 143.85, 130.30) and 4 aliphatic carbons; likely a carbonyl and two C=C carbons

support.quote:
Carbon NMR shows 7 distinct carbon signals:
- 161.40 ppm - likely carbonyl or aromatic C-O
- 143.85 ppm - likely aromatic or sp2 carbon
- 130.30 ppm - likely aromatic or sp2 carbon
- 26.65, 22.80, 21.35, 19.20 ppm - all aliphatic carbons (methyl groups)

nodes.text: Run mass spectrometry to determine molecular weight/formula
Mass spectrometry: base peak at m/z 127.09971
Run IR spectra to identify functional groups
IR indicates a carbonyl (1704 cm⁻¹), possible O-H (3505 cm⁻¹), and aromatic/sp2 C-H; combined with NMR suggests carbonyl and sp2 carbons with 4 methyl groups

support.quote:
IR spectra shows:
- 3505 cm⁻¹: O-H stretch (broad, likely alcohol or phenol)
- 3096-3007 cm⁻¹: C-H stretches (aromatic or sp2)
- 2996-2957 cm⁻¹: C-H stretches (aliphatic)
- 1704 cm⁻¹: C=O stretch (strong, likely ketone or aldehyde)

nodes.text: Search for C8H12O isomers to find candidate structures
List of C8H12O isomers obtained
Search for C9H16O isomers
List of C9H16O isomers obtained (MW=140, too high)
Run HSQC NMR to correlate H and C chemical shifts
The 6H singlet at 1.92 ppm is actually two distinct methyls (at δC 22.8 and 21.4); all 7 carbons are accounted for as 4 methyls + 3 quaternary carbons (161.40, 143.85, 130.30), consistent with C7H12O

support.quote:
So we have 4 distinct methyl groups:
- CH3 at δH 1.78, δC 19.2
- CH3 at δH 1.92, δC 22.8
- CH3 at δH 1.92, δC 21.4
- CH3 at δH 2.65, δC 26.6

And from ¹³C NMR, we also have:
- δC 161.40 (no H attached - quaternary, likely C=O)
- δC 143.85 (no H attached - quaternary sp2)
- δC 130.30 (no H attached - quaternary sp2)

So the structure has:
- 4 methyls (4 carbons, 12 H)
- 3 quaternary carbons (2 sp2, 1 carbonyl)
- Total: 7 carbons, 12 H, 1 O
